class.name: NetwIdentity
class.brief_description: A player identity an auth flow has already validated.
class.description: An auth provider returns this inside an [AuthResult]. The session treats [member username] as server-authoritative and stores the identity per peer. Access it through [member NetwParticipant.identity]. A session without an auth provider has no identities at all, and [member NetwParticipant.identity] returns [code]null[/code] there. It is not part of the replicated roster: [ResolvedJoin] is what the server sends to peers. [codeblock] func verify(data: PackedByteArray) -> AuthResult: var identity := NetwIdentity.new() identity.username = &"valeria" identity.external_id = "76561198000000000" identity.service = &"steam" return AuthResult.accept(identity) [/codeblock] The two statics are separate from all of that. They name a node for a human or for a log, and they work whether or not the session ever authenticated anyone.

method.name: stable_id_of
method.description: A key for [param node] that survives the node being rebuilt, for a debugger or a log that has to match rows across frames. It returns the peer [param node]'s entity represents when there is one, then the peer its name spells, and only then the node path, because a path changes when the node moves and the first two do not. A node that is not valid returns an empty [String].

method.name: username_of
method.description: A display name for [param node], for UI and logs. It returns the entity id [param node] was bound under when it has one, and otherwise the part of the node's name before the [code]|[/code] separator, which is where a bound name keeps it. A node that is not valid returns an empty [String].

members.member: The provider's own id for this player, such as a Steam id or a Discord user id.
Opaque provider data, forwarded as the provider gave it. Nothing in the session reads it.
The auth service that produced this identity.
The display name to spawn and show this player under. Server-authoritative, because an auth flow validated it rather than the peer asserting it.
